mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals labor market weakness that typically suppresses corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates sustained manufacturing output that supports equity market performance, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, INDPRO growth does not predict SPX 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 1.5% signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) above 145,000 indicates labor market strength that typically fuels consumer spending and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 145,000.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansions, joint monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signal accelerating consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansion, the joint increase of HOUST and RSAFS does not predict SPX 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% indicate cross-sector economic strength, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: When INDPRO and HOUST both increase > 0.5% in 1 month, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
